1. Employment does not establish regulatory eligibility.
2. Individual Engineer Registration does not establish office-classification membership.
3. Office-classification membership does not establish Responsible Engineer authority.
4. Only authority-recognized eligible engineers count toward discipline staffing.
5. Surplus recognized engineers are a deliberate compliance buffer.
6. A staffing shortage can escalate into loss of a discipline.
7. Replacing staff after discipline removal does not necessarily restore the discipline immediately.
8. Office category + permitted discipline + scope determine what AMEC is entitled to perform.
9. Every governed field on the official office registration has regulatory significance.
10. Office-registration changes and ordinary engineer-data updates are different regulatory workflows.
11. Responsible Engineer is a regulator-approved professional authority, not merely an organizational job title.
12. Multiple Responsible Engineers are allowed/used as operational resilience.
13. Removed Responsible Engineers must lose regulatory signature authority.
14. Official regulatory documents are superseded/versioned—not overwritten.
15. Government acceptance is separate from AMEC preparation/submission.
16. Human signature, stamp, final submission and authority acceptance remain human/external-authority actions.

1. The biggest missed requirement: discipline loss has a recovery lock
This is the most important correction.

He says that if the discipline is actually removed from the official office registration, AMEC may only be able to add that discipline back when the office registration is renewed. He gives the example that losing it shortly before renewal is manageable, while losing it early in a two-year cycle could leave AMEC waiting a very long time.
That means our previous state model was incomplete.
It cannot be just:
SHORTAGE → REPLACEMENT FOUND → COMPLIANT
It needs something closer to:
